Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service — Aria 3 recalibration

I told Dana on the Circle forum I’d write this up after my Aria 3 had been through a real trial. It has now made it through eight days of a civil trial, including a full day of expert testimony, so here’s my experience with Harbor Point Steno Service in Towson.

I dropped off my Stenvale Aria 3 on Monday, October 19, for a full recalibration, number bar sensor inspection, cleaning and firmware update. Harbor Point quoted $285 and estimated 10 business days. I picked it up Tuesday, October 27: six business days after drop-off. I paid $310 by card myself, as I do for all my equipment; there was no court reimbursement. The extra $25 was for an internal battery replacement. Gloria asked before doing that work, and I appreciated being given the choice.

The repair included a full keyboard recalibration, replacement of the number bar depression sensor, internal cleaning, a firmware update from 4.0.7 to 4.2.1 and the approved battery replacement. The invoice lists a 90-day warranty. The machine came back with a printed, one-page service sheet listing every adjustment. I’ve never had that from anyone else, and it’s useful to have a clear record of what was done.

Most important, the number bar behaved properly during the trial. On the first full day back, an engineer gave expert testimony in numbers all day. The number bar did not double a single stroke. That’s the kind of test I needed, and the Aria passed it.

There were two communication and loaner issues worth mentioning. I called Wednesday, October 21, to ask about progress. The call rang out, and there was no voicemail box set up. Gloria emailed me the following day, but I would have preferred a way to leave a message. Harbor Point’s phone hours are Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4. That’s the real weakness for anyone working a Monday docket or trying to reach the shop outside those hours.

A Stenvale Aria 2 loaner was offered, which helped while mine was in the shop. Its tilt arm slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition, so I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I mentioned it to Gloria, and she said they would repair the arm before lending it out again. I’m glad she took the report seriously, though the loaner was inconvenient that day.

Harbor Point is a two-person shop off York Road, with free parking in back. Gloria did good work on my machine, the turnaround was quicker than quoted, and $310 seems fair for the work done. I’d trust them with my Aria 3 again. Dana, based on my experience, I think you can trust them with your Aria too—just plan around the limited phone hours, and ask about a loaner if being without your machine would be a problem.
